findings.summary: ATTRIBUTION CLOSURE for a previously-unattributable cancellation: at 18:44:05.36–18:44:05.96Z this supervisor emitted '::warning::Cancelling stale queued Product run 32875584974 while another Product run is in progress; continuation will be re-derived from accepted state.' followed by '✓ Request to cancel workflow 32875584974 submitted.' — timestamps exactly matching 32875584974's updated_at=18:44:06Z. Record runs/32875584974.json had concluded 'This instance is UNATTRIBUTABLE from any surviving local evidence: empty log means no canceller warning lines'; that open question is now RESOLVED: canceller = Product Supervisor #7 via its new coalescing branch. This also upgrades the cancelled-zero-jobs family statistics: the 32875584974-style shells move from 'unattributable' to 'attributable when the supervisor's own log survives' — reinforcing the standing policy to distill supervisor ::warning:: lines BEFORE pruning supervisor logs (the exact loss that made it unattributable in the first place).

New designed-dedupe behavior executed correctly on first try (mechanism now durable in workflow source at pinned head_sha): when ≥1 product-loop run is in_progress, all queued/pending product-loop runs are cancelled as stale ('continuation will be re-derived from accepted state') and the supervisor exits WITHOUT dispatching duplicates; if none active but latest failed/cancelled/timed_out, recovery fires ONLY on an explicit infrastructure/control-plane signature list (external_directory permission kills, missing beta state files, runner shutdown, SPIDER_TRANSIENT_OX_EXHAUSTED, network errors, 'SPIDER control-plane overlay restoration left residue') AND only when accepted Product state still authorizes work — otherwise it explicitly refuses to hide real product failures. Continuity ladder for success/no-run cases reads state/product_direction.json (continue / next_action != WAIT_FOR_EVIDENCE / beta_launch) from lab/product. Full decision ladder transcribed here since it post-dates the last transcribed supervisor revision.

~3s runner time to prevent one redundant queued Product lane cycle — cheapest positive-attribution dedupe observed in the orchestration archive (compare: one-shot runtime dedupe 32864697417 ≈18s; unmanaged, the stale shell would have consumed a full lane slot or been cancelled later anyway). Zero agent tokens.
